newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Sun Alliance NZ operations make progress in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Sun Alliance NZ operations make progress in 1996.

text.p: Sun Alliance New Zealand Ltd said on Wednesday its fire and general insurance company, Sun Alliance Insurance Ltd, lifted its profit before tax by eight percent to NZ$21.6 million in the year to December 31, 1996.
It increased gross written premiums by 16 percent to $237 million.
The company's underwriting profit was up 83 percent to $18.4 million, and investment income up nine percent to $15.8 million.

"Competitive pressures in the corporate and commercial sectors resulted in across-the-board rate reductions. Sun Alliance was able to combat the decline in premiums this would have otherwise produced by holding key accounts and winning major new customers," the company said.
Sun Alliance said both Sun Alliance Insurance Ltd and Sun Alliance Life Ltd faced difficult trading conditions in the year.
"The investment, life and superannuation climate in the first half of the year was extremely difficult as the country moved towards its first election under the MMP system.

"It was not until the final quarter of the financial year that conditions changed, and in that period Sun Alliance Life Ltd set new records for itself with net new annualised premiums written," the company said.
After adjustment for the 1995 acquisition of the Oceanic Investment Bond business, Sun Alliance Life's year-on-year premiums were up three percent to $132 million.
Funds under management at year end stood at $825 million.
Sun Alliance in New Zealand will change its name to Royal & Sun Alliance this year, reflecting the international merger that took place in Britain last year.
